title: Mildred honest to a fault, not malicious
summary: Norvo says rumors about Mildred are untrue and that Dance should speak up; she was honest but never vicious.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: But, of course, any of those things, you know where there was any bad-mouthing, that is the thing that writers and people pick up, you know --
That's what they -- what they grab. They
grab those up.
It's something that --

And there's no really truth in it and you know, I hear a lot of these things. Sometimes I don't say anything, well what is the matter. But sometimes I wonder if I'm really doing the right thing by not saying something, because I think it should be set straight. I think it's a very -- I think that's a very poor blow to say about somebody that has no defense and to say it in such a context as that --
Yes, I do, too.
Because I know it isn't true.
Yeah.

Well, as a matter of fact, Red -- I mean that --
What?

Well I know Mildred was honest to a fault.
I know she was. That's where she made enemies sometimes.
I know she was honest. But she didn't
mean it -- she was honest, she didn't mean that --
To be mean --
Personal.
-- it was malicious.
